questions.label: 5(a)
questions.text:
Fig. No. 6 shows the details of Oldham’s coupling. Draw the following views of the assembly :
(i) Sectional Front View
(ii) Left hand Side View
[Parts: 1 Flange C.I. 2 off; 2 Central disc C.I. 1 off; 3 Shaft M.S. 2 off; 4 Taper key M.S. 2 off]
questions.marks_basis: group marks / number to attempt (not printed per sub-question)

misprint.doubt: In Fig. 6, the hub diameter is printed as “φ12D” and the flange keyway width as “28H7”. The key is 20 mm wide (20n6) and the shaft keyway is 20H7.
misprint.assumption: “φ12D” is read as Ø120 (2 × shaft diameter), and the flange keyway width is taken as 20 mm to suit the 20 mm key. The key length 96 is more than the 86 mm bore, so the key is shown projecting 10 mm beyond the hub.

questions.label: 5(b)
questions.text:
Fig. No. 7 shows details of lathe tool post. Draw the following views of assembly :
(i) Sectional FV
(ii) Top view
(iii) Prepare bill of material and indicate type of fit.
[Parts: 1 Post C.I.; 2 Block C.I.; 3 Ring C.I.; 4 Wedge M.S.; 5 Screw C.I.; each 1 off]
questions.marks_basis: group marks / number to attempt (not printed per sub-question)

misprint.doubt: In the tolerance chart the entry for 24H7 is printed as “+0.021 / +40.000” and the wedge size “24n8” in the chart but “24n6” on the drawing. The post carries “φ60H7” and the block hole “φ60e8”, which is the reverse of normal practice (capital letters are for holes).
misprint.assumption: 24H7 is taken as +0.021 / 0.000 and 24n6 (+0.036 / +0.015). The Ø60 hole (block) is taken as H7 and the Ø60 post as e8, so that the fit is a clearance fit; if taken literally as printed the hole would be smaller than the shaft.
